about: Every reader-facing sentence pattern in Bara, with {placeholders} that the code fills from real data. polish_wording.py sends this to an AI for plainer wording; a person reviews the suggestions before anything changes in site/js. Numbers never come from the AI.
audience: People living in Sarawak (Mukah and nearby), not data experts. Many read English as a second language. Reading age about 12.

items.where: Selected month panel, first sentence
items.template: Satellites spotted {n} hotspots in {area} in {month}.
items.example: Satellites spotted 216 hotspots in Mukah Division in July 2025.

items.where: Selected month, compares with a normal month
items.template: That is fewer than usual (a normal {mname} has about {median}).
items.example: That is fewer than usual (a normal October has about 15).

items.where: Selected month
items.template: That is about normal (a normal {mname} has about {median}).
items.example: That is about normal (a normal March has about 15).

items.where: Selected month
items.template: That is more than usual (a normal {mname} has about {median}).
items.example: That is more than usual (a normal May has about 40).

items.where: Selected month, at least twice normal
items.template: That is about {x} times more than usual (a normal {mname} has about {median}).
items.example: That is about 3 times more than usual (a normal July has about 64).

items.where: Selected month, months before 2012
items.template: This is an estimate, because the newer satellite only started in 2012.
items.example: This is an estimate, because the newer satellite only started in 2012.

items.where: Selected month, very recent months
items.template: Recent numbers may still change slightly.
items.example: Recent numbers may still change slightly.

items.where: Selected month without full data
items.template: There is no full satellite record for {area} in {month}.
items.example: There is no full satellite record for Mukah Division in January 2012.

items.where: 'What this means' for a month far above normal
items.template: A bad month for fires in {area}: far more than a normal {mname}. Months like this can bring smoky air.
items.example: A bad month for fires in Mukah Division: far more than a normal July. Months like this can bring smoky air.

items.where: 'What this means', above normal, during fire season
items.template: A busier fire-season month than usual in {area}. Watch haze news at times like this.
items.example: A busier fire-season month than usual in Sarawak. Worth keeping an eye on haze news at times like this.

items.where: 'What this means', above normal, outside fire season
items.template: More fires than a normal {mname} in {area}, even though this is usually a quieter time of year.
items.example: More fires than a normal April in Mukah Division, even though this is usually a quieter time of year.

items.where: 'What this means', normal, during fire season
items.template: A typical fire-season month for {area}: fires are common at this time of year, and this one was no worse than usual.
items.example: A typical fire-season month for Sarawak: fires are common at this time of year, and this one was no worse than usual.

items.where: 'What this means', normal, outside fire season
items.template: A typical {mname} for {area}: nothing unusual.
items.example: A typical March for Mukah Division: nothing unusual.

items.where: 'What this means', below normal, during fire season
items.template: Good news: a calmer fire season than usual in {area}.
items.example: Good news: a calmer fire season than usual in Sarawak.

items.where: 'What this means', below normal, outside fire season
items.template: Good news: fewer fires than usual in {area}, at an already quiet time of year.
items.example: Good news: fewer fires than usual in Mukah Division, at an already quiet time of year.

items.where: 'What this means', month without full data
items.template: There is no full satellite record for {month}, so we can't say how it compares.
items.example: There is no full satellite record for January 2012, so we can't say how it compares.

items.where: 'Be prepared' box: usual fire season of the area
items.template: In {area}, fire season usually runs {start} to {end}, busiest in {peak}.
items.example: In Mukah Division, fire season usually runs June to August, busiest in August.

items.where: 'Be prepared': today is inside fire season
items.template: It is {now} now, which is usually part of fire season.
items.example: It is August now, which is usually part of fire season.

items.where: 'Be prepared': fire season starts within 2 months
items.template: Fire season usually starts in {start}, so now is a good time to prepare.
items.example: Fire season usually starts in June, so now is a good time to prepare.

items.where: 'Be prepared': today is a quiet month
items.template: {now} is usually a quiet month for fires here.
items.example: November is usually a quiet month for fires here.

items.where: 'Be prepared': the picked month was busier than usual
items.template: {selected} was busier than usual. Fires nearby can bring haze.
items.example: July 2025 was busier than usual. Fires nearby can bring haze.

items.where: 'Be prepared': area with very few hotspots
items.template: Hotspots are rare in {area} itself.
items.example: Hotspots are rare in Tanjung Manis District itself.

items.where: 'Be prepared' checklist
items.template: Keep face masks (N95) at home for haze days.
items.example: Keep face masks (N95) at home for haze days.

items.where: 'Be prepared' checklist; APIMS is the official Malaysian air-quality site; 100 is the official 'unhealthy' level
items.template: Check today's air quality on APIMS (Department of Environment). Above 100 is unhealthy: spend less time outdoors.
items.example: Check today's air quality on APIMS (Department of Environment). Above 100 is unhealthy: spend less time outdoors.

items.where: 'Be prepared' checklist; 999 is Malaysia's emergency number
items.template: Do not burn rubbish or land. In an emergency, call 999.
items.example: Do not burn rubbish or land. In an emergency, call 999.

items.where: 'Be prepared' footnote
items.template: Based on past satellite records, not today's haze. Haze can also blow in from fires outside Sarawak.
items.example: Based on past satellite records, not today's haze. Haze can also blow in from fires outside Sarawak.

items.where: Forecast panel, first sentence
items.template: In {target}, expect about {n} hotspots in {area}.
items.example: In November 2026, expect about 39 hotspots in Sarawak.

items.where: Forecast panel, the likely range
items.template: Most likely somewhere between {low} and {high}.
items.example: Most likely somewhere between 25 and 84.

items.where: Forecast panel, when the number is the average of recent years
items.template: That is what recent {mname}s looked like.
items.example: That is what recent Novembers looked like.

items.where: Forecast panel, when the number comes from the trend model; {compare} is one of: more than / about the same as / fewer than / well above
items.template: That is {compare} recent {mname}s.
items.example: That is fewer than recent Novembers.

items.where: Forecast panel, rain in the two months before
items.template: The last two months had about normal rain.
items.example: The last two months had about normal rain.

items.where: Forecast panel
items.template: The last two months were drier than normal (about {pct}% less rain).
items.example: The last two months were drier than normal (about 20% less rain).

items.where: Forecast panel
items.template: The last two months were wetter than normal (about {pct}% more rain).
items.example: The last two months were wetter than normal (about 15% more rain).

items.where: Forecast 'What this means', expected is under a quarter of the busiest month
items.template: {mname} is usually a quiet month for fires in {area}.
items.example: November is usually a quiet month for fires in Sarawak.

items.where: Forecast 'What this means', middling
items.template: {mname} usually sees some fires in {area}, though not as many as the peak of fire season.
items.example: October usually sees some fires in Sarawak, though not as many as the peak of fire season.

items.where: Forecast 'What this means', near the peak
items.template: {mname} is one of the busiest fire months in {area}.
items.example: August is one of the busiest fire months in Sarawak.

items.where: Forecast 'What this means', added when a dry month would raise the number
items.template: A dry spell could push it up to about {dry}, so it is still worth being careful with open burning.
items.example: A dry spell could push it up to about 47, so it is still worth being careful with open burning.

items.where: Forecast 'What this means', when the dry case only adds a little
items.template: A dry spell would raise it a little, so it is still worth being careful with open burning.
items.example: A dry spell would raise it a little, so it is still worth being careful with open burning.

items.where: Forecast, heading over the three rain cases
items.template: Rain can change this
items.example: Rain can change this

items.where: Forecast, rain case label
items.template: If {mname} is drier than usual
items.example: If November is drier than usual

items.where: Forecast, rain case label
items.template: If {mname} has normal rain
items.example: If November has normal rain

items.where: Forecast, rain case label
items.template: If {mname} is wetter than usual
items.example: If November is wetter than usual

items.where: Forecast, under the rain cases
items.template: Less rain dries the land, so fires start and spread more easily.
items.example: Less rain dries the land, so fires start and spread more easily.

items.where: Forecast, when rain made little difference in the past
items.template: In past {mname}s, rain made little difference here.
items.example: In past Novembers, rain made little difference here.

items.where: Rain and hotspots chart 'What this means': the busiest month was a dry month
items.template: In {year}, the most hotspots were in {peak} ({n}). Rain was only {pct}% of normal that month. Dry weather and fires go together.
items.example: In 2019, hotspots peaked in August (1,320), when rain was only 69% of normal: a dry month. Dry weather and fires go together.

items.where: Rain chart: the busiest month had normal or more rain; {rainword} is 'about normal' or 'above normal'
items.template: In {year}, the most hotspots were in {peak} ({n}). Rain was {rainword}, so dry weather alone doesn't explain it.
items.example: In 2014, hotspots peaked in March (412), when rain was about normal, so dry weather alone doesn't explain that peak.

items.where: Rain chart: almost no hotspots that year
items.template: Very few hotspots in {year}, so rain made little visible difference.
items.example: Very few hotspots in 2022, so rain made little visible difference.

items.where: Rain chart, how to read it
items.template: How to read it: the red line shows hotspots each month. The bars show rain that month. The black tick is a normal amount. Orange bars are dry months, and dry months often bring more hotspots.
items.example: How to read it: red line = hotspots each month. Bars: rain that month (the black tick is a normal amount). Orange bars are dry months, and dry months often come with more hotspots.

items.where: Sensor proof 'What this means', why the satellite fix matters
items.template: An old satellite and a new one count fires differently. The new one sees about {ratio} times more. Without the fix, fires would seem to jump suddenly in 2012. With the fix, all 25 years can be compared fairly.
items.example: An older and a newer satellite count fires differently: the newer one sees about 4 times more. Without this fix, fires would seem to jump suddenly in 2012. With it, all 25 years can be compared fairly.

items.where: Sensor proof 'What this means'; years before 2012 are estimates
items.template: {area} had the most hotspots in {year}: about {n} (estimated, because the new satellite started in 2012).
items.example: Sarawak's worst year was 2009, with about 22,249 hotspots (estimated, as the newer satellite started in 2012).

items.where: Sensor proof 'What this means', long-term change
items.template: Recent years ({from} to {to}) had about {pct}% fewer hotspots a year than {from0} to {to0}.
items.example: In recent years (2021 to 2025) there were about 84% fewer hotspots a year than in 2001 to 2010.

items.where: Map, under the map
items.template: Darker squares had more hotspots. {area} is outlined.
items.example: Darker squares had more hotspots. Mukah Division is outlined.

items.where: Calendar, under the title
items.template: Each box is one month. Darker = more hotspots. Click a box to see that month.
items.example: Each box is one month. Darker = more hotspots. Click a box to see that month.

items.where: Commander mode 'What happened': player's trucks reached the 5 worst fire areas faster than the computer's coverage plan
items.template: Your trucks got to the worst fires faster than the computer's plan ({mine} against {plan} on average).
items.example: Your trucks reached the worst fires faster than the computer's plan (17 km against 29 km on average).

items.where: Commander mode 'What happened': about as fast as the computer's plan
items.template: Your trucks got to the worst fires about as fast as the computer's plan ({mine} against {plan} on average).
items.example: Your trucks reached the worst fires about as fast as the computer's plan (27 km against 29 km on average).

items.where: Commander mode 'What happened': slower than the computer's plan
items.template: Your trucks took longer to get to the worst fires than the computer's plan ({mine} against {plan} on average).
items.example: Your trucks took longer to reach the worst fires than the computer's plan (41 km against 29 km on average).

items.where: Commander mode: the worst fire area had a truck within 20 km
items.template: The worst fire area, with {n} hotspots, was only {km} from a truck.
items.example: The worst fire area, with 146 hotspots, was only 8 km from a truck.

items.where: Commander mode: the worst fire area had no truck within 20 km
items.template: The worst fire area, with {n} hotspots, had no truck nearby: the nearest was {km} away.
items.example: The worst fire area, with 146 hotspots, had no truck nearby: the nearest was 34 km away.

items.where: Commander mode: one other fire area had no truck within 20 km, so a truck came from further
items.template: Fire area {areas} had no truck nearby, so a truck came from {kms} away.
items.example: Fire area 4 had no truck nearby, so a truck came from 37 km away.

items.where: Commander mode: several fire areas had no truck within 20 km; {areas} is like '4 and 5', {kms} like '37 km and 24 km'
items.template: Fire areas {areas} had no truck nearby, so trucks came from {kms} away.
items.example: Fire areas 4 and 5 had no truck nearby, so trucks came from 37 km and 24 km away.

items.where: Commander mode: share of all hotspots within 20 km of a truck
items.template: Your trucks were within 20 km of {pct} out of 100 hotspots (computer plan: {planpct}).
items.example: Your trucks were within 20 km of 77 out of every 100 hotspots (the computer's plan: 90).

items.where: Commander mode tip, when some fire area needed a long trip
items.template: Tip: put a truck closer to fire area {rank}, the longest trip.
items.example: Tip: place a truck closer to fire area 4, the longest trip.

items.where: Commander mode tip, when trucks covered clearly fewer hotspots than the computer's plan
items.template: Tip: spread your trucks out a little to cover more of the smaller fires.
items.example: Tip: spread your trucks out a little to cover more of the smaller fires.

items.where: Commander mode, when every worst fire area had a truck within 20 km
items.template: Well placed: every worst fire area had a truck nearby.
items.example: Well placed: every worst fire area had a truck nearby.
